title: Time interval fields: days, minutes and the single window

fields.statement: A time interval has five fields: a system-generated integer `id`, a `name`, integer `startTime` and `endTime`, and a `daysOfWeek` list.

expect.description: System-generated identifier for the time interval
Name to identify the time interval

minutes-from-midnight.statement: `startTime` and `endTime` are minutes from midnight, 0 to 1439 (480 is 08:00, 1020 is 17:00), not clock strings. The OpenAPI document says only "start time" and "end time"; the unit comes from the MCP server's tool description and the SDK example.

days-values.statement: `daysOfWeek` takes ANY, NONE, EVERYDAY, SUN, MON, TUE, WED, THU, FRI and SAT; EVERYDAY selects all seven days. The Python docstring and the MCP tool description list EVERYDAY and the seven day names without ANY or NONE; the Terraform time window data source's `day_of_week` lists ANY and NONE as well.

expect.description: Specifies which days of the week apply to the time interval. If set to EVERYDAY, all the days of the week are chosen.

quotes: Days: EVERYDAY, SUN, MON, TUE, WED, THU, FRI, SAT. List or JSON string.

one-period.statement: An interval holds one time period applied to its chosen days; the console allows only one period at a time. A split shift (08:00 to 12:00 and 14:00 to 18:00) therefore needs two intervals.
one-period.conditions: The one-period limit is stated by the Help page; the two-interval remedy is inference from the schema and the rule field being a list (zia.time-intervals.rule-usage).

quotes: Only one time period can be set at a time.

weekly-recurrence-only.statement: The only recurrence is the weekly one given by `daysOfWeek`; the object has no date, exclusion or calendar field.
weekly-recurrence-only.conditions: Absence from the five-field schema and the console drawer.

go-starttime-always-sent.statement: In the Go SDK `startTime` has no `omitempty` while `endTime`, `id`, `name` and `daysOfWeek` do, so a zero start (midnight) is always sent and a zero end is dropped from the body. The Python model sends all five unconditionally.

string-times.title: What the API does with HH:MM strings for startTime and endTime
string-times.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Code that passes string values (e.g. \"08:00\") will fail or produce unexpected results." The API schema types both fields as integers, but no source shows the response to a string. The Python SDK docstring itself passes quoted minute strings ('0', '1439'). Resolve by posting a string time to a scratch tenant.
